answer: Grade agents on unseen tasks that change every epoch, giving each identity a different held-out set, and count reward only when its score clears a rising bar over consecutive epochs, like a signal that must grow clearer rather than merely repeat. A wharf can berth one real ship at a time, and here one capable model can genuinely pass only one identity's set per epoch: a farm minting copies has no cheap shortcut, because copied answers fail on tasks its clones never saw, and quartz-clear grading leaves no room to bluff.
